text:
maria: heads up — we see a slow-but-steady memory climb on the streaming-chat pods when sessions hit ~60k tokens. Heap grows over hours rather than spikes. attaching quick flame output in case useful

sam: ugh, saw something similar in canary yesterday. looks like KV residency keeps increasing even after session end?

maria: exact. kv_resident_pages increases monotonically in the metrics. eviction rate stays low. no OOMs but usable memory keeps dropping.

jin: can you paste the profiler slice? curious if there are long-lived refs from tool-loop handlers or lingered batch ops.

maria: pasted below — this is a sampled heap diff between 2h and 6h of the same process (cropped):
```
+ 42% kv_slot_table (n=312k)
+ 18% session_ctx (n=48k)
+ 10% thread_local_cache (n=8k)
-  5% transient_buffers
```
Looks like kv_slot_table growth is dominant.

alex: are these pages pinned or just marked resident? If pinning, could be a leak where page refs don't drop. If just resident, maybe compaction/sweep frequency too low.

maria: metrics show "kv_page_pinned_count" spikes correlate with long chats and never fully decay. eviction_attempts is non-zero but eviction_success is low.

sam: hypothesis: prefix-KV caching plus batching heuristic is pinning pages when requests stream partial prefixes; the page touch pattern prevents eviction because LRU window is effectively sliding.

jin: can we repro locally with a long-tool-loop harness? run 1000 concurrent sessions each doing small-turn streaming for 4k tokens per turn for 500 turns and enable debug knobs: `KV_FORCE_EVICT=0.1 KV_COMPACT_INTERVAL=60`

maria: started a run on bench-5 (pid 4421). gathering `malloc_stats`, `kv:stats`, and our custom `page-trace` which logs `PIN/UNPIN` ops. sharing tail:
```
[13:12:00] PID 4421 page-trace: PIN page_id=0x3e5d count=1 session=0x7f3
[13:12:01] PID 4421 page-trace: PIN page_id=0x3e6a count=1 session=0x7f4
... (repeats) ...
[16:14:12] PID 4421 page-trace: UNPIN page_id=0x3e5d count=0 session=0x7f3
```
We see many PIN without corresponding UNPIN for pages tied to tool-loop sessions.

alex: sounds like a missing UNPIN on session termination or tool-handler exception path. Check `session_close()` callsites and any early `return` paths. Also verify RAII wrappers in C++ side — destructors must call `unpin()` when TLS freed.

sam: also check batching path: when we merge partial requests into a batch, we increase page refcounts for the whole batch. if the batch is canceled (timeout or backpressure), failure path might skip decrement. Look at `batch_coalesce()` error branch.

jin: i dug a bit — found `if (!batch.scheduled()) return;` in `batch_coalesce()` which returns without decrementing `page_ref->hold_for_batch`. adding a guard to decrement solves the immediate repro locally.

maria: amazing — patched that in bench run. memory curve flattened after ~30m. eviction success went from 12%->78% on the run.

ops-bot: deploy log — canary build `kv-fix/batch-unpin` rolled to bench-5 at 17:02 UTC. monitor for 3h.

alex: nice catch. followups:
- add unit test that simulates batch cancellation and asserts refcounts return to zero
- add a debug-mode periodic refcount audit that logs suspicious pages with net>0 refs after session gc
- evaluate whether compaction frequency should be increased when long-stream density > threshold

sam: also add metric for `batch_cancellation_count` to correlate to spikes.

maria: will open PR with fix+test+metric. leaving the bench run on for a couple hours then pushing to canary cluster if stable. thanks all. :pray:

jin: quick note — this does suggest kernel selection interacts: some optimized kernels hold intermediate buffers longer for fused ops; ensure those codepaths also unpin on early exit. I'll audit kernels used by the streaming path.

maria: good call. I'll include a note in the PR and tag eng-runtime-kernel team.

alex: excellent triage. great small fix with high impact.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inference/+/4231 — includes patch, unit, and metric. moving to canary in ~1h. :rocket:
